newsitem.title: ITALY: Pirelli profits double, more progress ahead.
newsitem.headline: Pirelli profits double, more progress ahead.

text.p: Italian tyre and cable group Pirelli on Thursday announced a near-doubling of first half profits as its tyre business rebounded back to health and its cables operations continued to thrive and grow.

The Milan-based company said first-half 1996 consolidated net profits rose to 206 billion lire ($136 million) from 115 billion despite half-year overall sales falling some 3.5 percent to 5.37 trillion lire.

Pirelli said it now expected better results for 1996 compared with 1995 in the year when the group showed net consolidated profits of 304 billion lire, a result which itself doubled from 1994 on annual sales up 11 percent.

"We have all the means to be able to continue the course that is starting to give positive results," said group managing director Marco Trochetti Provera at a news conference to announce the half-year results.
Analysts said the results were led by the rapid recovery in the tyre business, but also showed solid underlying progress in its specialist cables business around the world.

The group's automotive tyre interests grouped under Amsterdam-listed Pirelli-Tyre, and 81 percent owned by Pirelli SpA, showed a profits leap, while it also looked forward to further improvements in the second half of 1996.
Tyre first half net profits rose to 55.4 million guilders from 10.7 million guilders on a turnover up 8.6 percent.
"The expectation is that the positive trend in results will continue in the second half, to the same degree as the market," Pirelli-Tyre said in a statement.

Pirelli cables continued to make progress around the world and its future prospects were highlighted by the announcement of its long-awaited Chinese joint venture last month to tap Chinese growth in the rapidily-growing Chinese telecommunications market. ($1=1,519 lire)
